overview.summary: Bakers make bread, pastries, cakes and other baked goods, from small bakeries to large production lines.
overview.problems: They provide fresh, safe, tasty baked foods and keep quality consistent, often starting very early in the morning.
overview.worksWith: Bakery staff, pastry chefs, shop and delivery staff, suppliers and customers.
overview.workplaces: Bakeries, supermarkets, hotels, restaurants and food factories, and some bakers run their own shops.

timeline.title: Mixing and shaping dough
timeline.description: The baker measures ingredients, mixes dough and shapes loaves or rolls.

timeline.title: Baking
timeline.description: The baker loads the ovens, watches time and temperature and takes the baked goods out at the right moment.
timeline.why: Small timing errors change the result.

timeline.title: Finishing and displaying
timeline.description: The baker decorates pastries and cakes, packs orders and stocks the shelves.
timeline.why: Look matters as well as taste.

timeline.title: Customers and orders
timeline.description: The baker serves customers or prepares special orders, such as celebration cakes.

timeline.title: Cleaning and food safety
timeline.description: The baker cleans equipment and checks hygiene and temperatures.

timeline.title: Planning and ordering
timeline.description: The baker orders ingredients, plans tomorrow's batches and prepares doughs that rest overnight.
timeline.why: Planning keeps ingredients fresh and waste low.

responsibilities: Mixing, shaping and baking products to a consistent standard
Following food safety and hygiene rules
challenges: Starts are very early, often in the middle of the night.
Ovens are hot and the work is physically demanding, including lifting heavy sacks.
Tasks are repetitive and involve long periods standing.
Burns, cuts and flour dust are risks managed by careful habits.
Busy periods come before festivals and holidays.
Profit margins are small in some bakeries.
Pay can be modest early on in many places.
workEnvironment: Bakeries and kitchens that are warm, floury and busy, often starting before dawn. The work is physical and detailed, and many bakers work in small teams. Hours often include early mornings, weekends and holidays.
rewards: The satisfaction of a finished loaf
The option to open your own bakery
tradeoffs: Pay and conditions that vary by country and employer

activity.title: Bake a simple recipe and change one thing
steps: With an adult, choose a simple recipe such as plain biscuits or bread rolls.
Measure the ingredients carefully and write down the baking time and temperature.
Bake a first batch and note how it looks and tastes.
Change one thing, such as the baking time by a minute, and bake a second batch.
Compare the results and note whether the precise work felt enjoyable.
activity.outcome: You practise measuring accurately, changing one variable at a time and learning from results.
activity.safety: Always bake with an adult, use oven gloves, keep hot trays away from children and pets, wash your hands, and check for food allergies before sharing.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
